correctness.rationale: The archival projective principal-minor map is \(\operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb C)^n\)-invariant. A generic diagonal cocharacter with powers-of-two weights has exactly the \(2^n\) coordinate tensor lines as ambient fixed points. For diagonal \(A,B\), the map is the Segre monomial map, so every coordinate tensor point is actually in the variety. Thus the variety has exactly \(2^n\) fixed points. Algebraic \(\mathbb C^*\)-localization of compactly supported Euler characteristic and projectivity give \(\chi_{\mathrm{top}}=2^n\). Additivity then makes the ambient complement have \(\chi_c=0\). The packaged checker independently verifies weight separation and every coordinate-point diagonal specialization on substantial finite ranges.

value.rationale: The projective principal-minor variety is a classical and technically difficult algebraic variety: even its first nontrivial case has a large degree-12 defining ideal and appears as a distinguished hyperdeterminant singular-locus component. The theorem determines a canonical global invariant uniformly in all dimensions and shows a striking cancellation: despite being a proper high-codimension singular subvariety for \(n\ge4\), it retains the full ambient Euler characteristic, forcing its complement to have compactly supported Euler characteristic zero. The result applies to the general nonsymmetric principal-minor variety, not merely the previously treated symmetric subvariety, and directly connects the archival \(\operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb C)^n\) symmetry to global topology.
